Welcome, Young Scientists!

Discover how scientists observe sounds, describe what they notice, share ideas, and use science equipment safely. Explore each card, try the activities, and explain your thinking.

2

Explore the Scientific and Manipulative Skills

These cards follow the Year 1 source sheet. Click one card at a time to explore the example, think about the question, and talk about your answer with your teacher or classmates.

SCIENCE PROCESS SKILLS

Science Content (Example)

Pupils listen to the sound of a musical instrument, then observe which instrument is correct.

Thinking Skill: Attributing

Process auditory information received through the ears while the eyes are closed.

Thinking Skill: Comparing and Contrasting

Examples: cymbals, maracas, wood block, triangle and castanet.

Science Content (Example)

Pupils talk about the sheep model they have constructed.

Thinking Skill: Relating

Identify similarities and differences between the constructed sheep model and a picture of a real sheep.

Thinking Skill: Comparing and Contrasting

Compare the physical appearance of the real sheep and the constructed model.

Thinking Skill: Analysing

Break down the sheep model into parts: body, head, legs and connections.

Thinking Skill: Making Conclusion

Use observations to judge how well the model represents a real sheep.

MANIPULATIVE SKILLS

Science Content (Example)

Use and handle a magnifying glass and cutter correctly and safely while observing the onion’s surface and internal layers.

Mental Action

Determine the correct object distance and magnifying-glass position for a clear image.

Safety reminder: A teacher or responsible adult must handle the cutter.

Science Content (Example)

Pupils cut the onion using a cutter.

Mental Action

Think about how to handle living organisms and specimens carefully without damaging or harming them.

Safety reminder: Pupils should not use a cutter independently.

Science Content (Example)

Pupils sketch and label the pattern of an onion.

Mental Action

Visualise the object being cut and predict the shape of its cross-section before drawing it.

Science Content (Example)

Pupils wash the cutter after the experiment.

Mental Action

Recall correct cleaning procedures and check that equipment is free of residue without causing damage.

Science Content (Example)

Pupils store the cutter and magnifying glass in their proper places.

Mental Action

Categorise equipment and evaluate safety factors to choose a stable, safe storage location.
